stem: Besides myocarditis, which of the following sets of complications is associated with diphtheria?

options.label: A
options.misconception: None — polyneuropathy, nephritis, and thrombocytopenia accompany myocarditis in diphtheria.
options.explanation: CDC lists myocarditis, polyneuropathies, nephritis, and thrombocytopenia among the complications of diphtheria.

options.label: B
options.misconception: Confuses diphtheria with mumps, whose complications include orchitis and pancreatitis.
options.explanation: Orchitis, pancreatitis, and aseptic meningitis are classic complications of mumps, a paramyxovirus infection, not diphtheria.

options.label: C
options.text: Cataracts, deafness, and patent ductus arteriosus
options.misconception: Confuses diphtheria with congenital rubella syndrome.
options.explanation: Cataracts, deafness, and patent ductus arteriosus make up congenital rubella syndrome after maternal rubella infection in pregnancy.

options.label: D
options.text: Trismus, opisthotonos, and generalized muscle spasms
options.misconception: Confuses diphtheria with tetanus, another toxin-mediated vaccine-preventable disease.
options.explanation: Trismus, opisthotonos, and muscle spasms are tetanus features: tetanospasmin blocks inhibitory neurotransmitter release in the spinal cord.

options.label: E
options.text: Splenic rupture, hemolytic anemia, and hepatitis
options.misconception: Confuses diphtheria with infectious mononucleosis, which also causes pharyngitis.
options.explanation: Splenic rupture, hemolytic anemia, and hepatitis are complications of Epstein-Barr virus infectious mononucleosis, not diphtheria.

context: Learning objective: Complications of diphtheria include myocarditis, polyneuropathies, nephritis, and thrombocytopenia.
